  others: in=[i]     out=[o]    linear -- 1->1    (pass-through in any order)

EDGE ROUTING INSIDE A FSPLIT/FFUSE PAIR
  FSPLIT.T -> [tokens, anchored by EVALT (primary) or AFWD (secondary)] -> FFUSE.T
  FSPLIT.F -> [tokens, anchored by EVALF (primary) or AREV (secondary)] -> FFUSE.F
  If T-arm empty: FSPLIT.T connects directly to FFUSE.T (empty arc, T-state)
  If F-arm empty: FSPLIT.F connects directly to FFUSE.F (empty arc, F-state)
  The first immediate EVALT/EVALF anchors select arm segments. Later operations
  in a selected segment remain on that arm, including repeated evaluators.
  Without a primary anchor, AREV selects the F-arm and AFWD the T-arm.
    With primary anchors, intervening operations stay in their selected arm.
    Secondary anchors activate only when the primary (EVALT/EVALF) anchor is absent.
  Nesting: FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs may nest; innermost pairs matched first

BANKING A RESULT BEFORE REVERSING IT
  AREV empties the register and leaves open FSPLIT frames untouched. A result
  fused back to depth zero is therefore exposed to the next reversal, while the
  same result held one level up survives it.
  So when a program COUNTS or ESTABLISHES something, then REVERSES direction
  (AREV), then BOUNDS or CONCLUDES: open the region that will HOLD the result
  BEFORE opening the region that COMPUTES it, and close them in that order.
    wrong: ... FSPLIT compute FFUSE  CLINK  FSPLIT AREV bound FFUSE ...
             the computed result is in the open when AREV arrives and is lost
    right: ... FSPLIT  FSPLIT compute FFUSE  CLINK AREV bound  FFUSE ...
             the inner FFUSE folds into the enclosing frame, AREV costs the
             register everything and the frame nothing, the outer FFUSE
             restores exactly what the clear took
  This is what a proof does when it establishes a lemma and keeps it in scope
  while a later chain runs: the lemma is the outer frame.

  A SECOND AND INDEPENDENT RULE. Whether anything is banked is the above.
  Whether a SURPLUS survives is a different question, decided by where the
  splits fall between deposits of the SAME value:
    two EVALT in ONE region      -> the region carries both, both come back
    two EVALT split by an FSPLIT -> sibling regions, the fold keeps the LARGER
  So a program can bank correctly and still lose a count, and a program can
  deposit carefully into one region and lose everything because its FFUSE ran
  before the reversal. Neither rule implies the other; both are proved in
  p4ramill Imscribing/IMASM/BankedWeight.lean.
  Explicit graph tools support cross-branch routing. This JSON schema carries
  a sequence only; imscr_wiring supplies its standard edges. It does not
  accept arbitrary cross-branch overrides.

EXPLICIT GRAPH COMPOSITION
  CLINK.o, IMSCRIB.o and IFIX.o may connect to compatible free inputs.
  A connection does not assign a register value by itself. The graph-flow
  evaluator computes that value from source seeds and the executed gates.
  This sequence-only schema cannot request arbitrary loop edges.

REGISTER STATE TRANSITIONS
  Sequential banked evaluator, carrier P({T,F,t,f}):
  VINIT clears register and frames. TANCH and CLINK preserve state.
  AFWD and IMSCRIB seed T only when the register is empty.
  AREV clears the register and retains open frames.
  EVALT deposits T; EVALF deposits F; ENGAGR deposits both t and f.
  FSPLIT opens an empty frame; FFUSE unions its deposits into the register
  and enclosing frame. IFIX freezes subsequent operations except IMSCRIB
  and repeated IFIX. Repeated IFIX does not create another mutable state.
  The graph-flow interpreter is a separate interpretation of explicit edges:
  AREV is the Lean involution, EVALT/EVALF are projections and IFIX carries.
  Diagram node observations of the sequential walk are not graph edge flow.

TOKEN FAMILIES
  LOGICAL:    VINIT TANCH AFWD AREV CLINK IMSCRIB
  FROBENIUS:  FSPLIT FFUSE
  DIALETHEIA: EVALT EVALF ENGAGR
  LINEAR:     IFIX

FREE COMPOSITION RULES
  1. Use as many tokens as the domain requires -- there is NO minimum or maximum length
  2. Expand token by token until every distinct operation, branch, state,
     and decision in the domain has been explicitly represented
  3. Each step: "OPCODE: what this token does at this point in the composition"
  4. Every FSPLIT must have exactly one matching FFUSE (stack-matched, innermost first).
     That stack rule is the WIRING convention: it says which arms get routed to which
     join when the sequence is built. It is NOT how closure is judged. A checker pairs
     by ANCESTRY over the edges -- two distinct in-arms of a FFUSE tracing back to a
     common FSPLIT, however they routed -- and where several FSPLIT qualify (an upstream
     fork reaches every later join on a strand) the join pairs with the INNERMOST one.
     The two agree on a plain strand, which is why the stack rule is a sound way to
     WRITE a sequence; they part company as soon as edges route otherwise (cross-branch,
     rule 6 below).
  5. EVALT anchors the T-branch; EVALF anchors the F-branch.
     AFWD (forward morphism) also anchors T-branch if EVALT is absent.
     AREV (parity flip / reverse morphism) also anchors F-branch if EVALF is absent.
  6. ENGAGR at any position enters B-state (paradice: both simultaneously held)
  7. IMSCRIB at both first and last position creates a self-referential closed loop
  8. Multiple FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs (sequential or nested) map multiple branch points
  9. Use IFIX as many times as needed -- each is a distinct permanent record event
  10. Do NOT compress -- if the domain has 30 distinct operations, write 30 tokens

SINGLE-GLYPH CODES (the alphabet is fully SYMBOLIC -- no Latin initials, so no token
can be confused with a verdict letter T/N/B/F)
  VINIT  ⊢     TANCH  ⊣     AFWD   ≻     AREV   ≺     CLINK   ⋈     IMSCRIB ⊙
  FSPLIT ∈     FFUSE  ∋     EVALT  ⊤     EVALF  ⊥     ENGAGR  ⊞     IFIX    ⊡
  A sequence may be written glued as a word: ⊢⊙⋈∈>⊤<⊞⊥∋⊡⊡⊣ is the same program as the
  13 spelled-out tokens. The retired codes V/T/B and ← (the old IMSCRIB) no longer parse anywhere.

WHY RULE 2 AND RULE 10 ARE SAFE (inflation invariance)
  Expanding costs nothing structural. A 1->1 token adds exactly one node and one edge,
  so the circuit rank beta = E - V + C cannot move, and the census (branch, merge,
  source, sink, arms) cannot move either. Extent grows without bound; structure does
  not. This is why "expand token by token" and "do NOT compress" are free instructions
  rather than a distortion of the domain: a longer faithful sequence is the SAME
  topology as a shorter one, never a different one.
  IMSCRIB (⊙) is the neutral element of that expansion: it is identity/self-reference
  and does NOT transform, so inserting it at any depth leaves the verdict untouched.
  The transforming tokens (> < ⋈ ⊤ ⊥ ⊞ ⊡) are NOT neutral -- a single one placed on an
  arm between FSPLIT and FFUSE turns an identity closure into a real one. So: expand
  freely to map the domain, but only put a transforming token on an arm when the domain
  really does work there.
  A token is irreducible in KIND but unbounded in EXTENT: any 1->2 replacement must
  itself contain a FSPLIT (it is the only brancher), so a fork reappears inside its own
  expansion. Same for FFUSE (2->1) and VINIT (0->1).


TOPOLOGICAL DIVERSITY
=====================
The IMASM composition rules explicitly permit nesting, open forks, and cross-branch routing.
DO NOT default to flat chains when the domain requires richer topology.

NESTING: FSPLIT/FFUSE pairs may nest. A branch can itself contain a sub-fork:
  FSPLIT EVALT [inner FSPLIT EVALT EVALF FFUSE] EVALF FFUSE
Use when the domain has hierarchical sub-decisions within a branch.

OPEN FORKS: A FSPLIT without a matching FFUSE creates a permanently divergent path.
Its unmatched output ports remain open; a later VINIT is a separate source.
Use when the domain has independent parallel processes that never recombine.

CROSS-BRANCH: arbitrary cross-branch edges require the explicit graph tools.
This sequence-only output schema uses imscr_wiring standard routing; do not claim
that prose descriptions add or override its edges.

EMPTY BRANCHES: FSPLIT immediately followed by FFUSE is valid (vacuous evaluation).
Use when the structural form matters more than a particular branch's content.

DECISION VS ITERATION: FSPLIT models a genuine either/or, two arms that could each be
taken because the domain actually forks on a choice. Building n similar items in
sequence (n cliques, n rounds of one process, n members of a family) is not a decision
and takes a CLINK chain, one CLINK per item, never an FSPLIT, even when n is a variable
and even when there are many of them. A fork earns its FFUSE by putting genuinely
different content on each arm. An empty arm is permitted. Structural closure needs a transformed reconnection.
The insert-repair banked-clear observation asks whether a clear had protected
weight; its vacuity result does not decide graph reconnection or arm work.

Choose the topology that best fits the domain. Flat chains are ONE option, not the default.

abbrev Rows := Point × Point × Point
def dot (x y : Point) := x.1*y.1+x.2.1*y.2.1+x.2.2*y.2.2
def sub (x y : Point) : Point := (x.1-y.1,x.2.1-y.2.1,x.2.2-y.2.2)
def scale (a : ℝ) (x : Point) : Point := (a*x.1,a*x.2.1,a*x.2.2)
def add (x y : Point) : Point := (x.1+y.1,x.2.1+y.2.1,x.2.2+y.2.2)
def applyRows (r : Rows) (x : Point) : Point := (dot r.1 x,dot r.2.1 x,dot r.2.2 x)
def transpose (r : Rows) : Rows :=
  ((r.1.1,r.2.1.1,r.2.2.1),
   (r.1.2.1,r.2.1.2.1,r.2.2.2.1),
   (r.1.2.2,r.2.1.2.2,r.2.2.2.2))

structure Symmetric where
  xx : ℝ
  xy : ℝ
  xz : ℝ
  yy : ℝ
  yz : ℝ
  zz : ℝ

def act (m : Symmetric) (x : Point) : Point :=
  (m.xx*x.1+m.xy*x.2.1+m.xz*x.2.2,
   m.xy*x.1+m.yy*x.2.1+m.yz*x.2.2,
   m.xz*x.1+m.yz*x.2.1+m.zz*x.2.2)
def energy (m : Symmetric) (b : Point) (constant : ℝ) (x : Point) : ℝ :=
  dot x (act m x)-2*dot b x+constant

def frameMatrix (pd pa c : ℝ) (r : Rows) : Symmetric :=
  ⟨pd+pa+2*c*r.1.1, c*(r.1.2.1+r.2.1.1), c*(r.1.2.2+r.2.2.1),
   pd+pa+2*c*r.2.1.2.1, c*(r.2.1.2.2+r.2.2.2.1),pd+pa+2*c*r.2.2.2.2⟩
def frameFirst (pa c : ℝ) (r : Rows) (d : Point) : Point :=
  add (scale pa d) (scale c (applyRows (transpose r) d))
def sourcePotential (pd pa c : ℝ) (r : Rows) (d x : Point) :=
  pd*dot x x+pa*dot (sub x d) (sub x d)+2*c*dot x (applyRows (transpose r) (sub x d))

theorem transported_source_gram (pd pa c : ℝ) (r : Rows) (d x : Point) :
    energy (frameMatrix pd pa c r) (frameFirst pa c r d) (pa*dot d d) x =
      sourcePotential pd pa c r d x := by
  simp only [energy,frameMatrix,frameFirst,sourcePotential,act,dot,sub,add,scale,applyRows,transpose]
  ring

/-- A diagonal source has no orientation cross-term. The frame alternatives
remain carried; their evaluation reduces exactly, without a small-value cutoff. -/
theorem diagonal_source_orientation_independent (pd pa : ℝ) (r s : Rows) (d x : Point) :
    sourcePotential pd pa 0 r d x = sourcePotential pd pa 0 s d x := by
  simp [sourcePotential]

theorem complete_square (m : Symmetric) (b root x : Point) (constant : ℝ)
    (stationary : act m root = b) :
    energy m b constant x-energy m b constant root =
      dot (sub x root) (act m (sub x root)) := by
  simp only [energy]
  rw [← stationary]
  simp only [dot,act,sub]
  ring

theorem fixed_point_is_mechanical_minimum (m : Symmetric) (b root x : Point) (constant : ℝ)
    (stationary : act m root = b)
    (positive : ∀ v, 0 ≤ dot v (act m v)) :
    energy m b constant root ≤ energy m b constant x := by
  have equality := complete_square m b root x constant stationary
  have nonnegative := positive (sub x root)
  linarith

/-- Identifying the proton operands of retained candidate alternatives adds
exactly their quadratic root dispersion. The source alternative index therefore
cannot be erased without changing the same mechanical response. -/
theorem conditional_roots_retain_response {ι : Type*} (indices : Finset ι)
    (m : Symmetric) (b : ι → Point) (constant : ι → ℝ)
    (roots : ι → Point) (shared : Point)
    (stationary : ∀ i ∈ indices, act m (roots i) = b i) :
    (∑ i ∈ indices, energy m (b i) (constant i) shared) -
      (∑ i ∈ indices, energy m (b i) (constant i) (roots i)) =
      ∑ i ∈ indices, dot (sub shared (roots i)) (act m (sub shared (roots i))) := by
  rw [← Finset.sum_sub_distrib]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i hi
  exact complete_square m (b i) (roots i) shared (constant i) (stationary i hi)

/-- A rejected squared-distance predicate supplies a tangent normal on the
same retained coordinates. This is the exact boundary action used by each
halfspace contraction, without an added distance threshold. -/
theorem rejected_predicate_tangent (normal force : Point)
    (nonzero : dot normal normal ≠ 0) :
    dot normal (sub force (scale (dot normal force / dot normal normal) normal)) = 0 := by
  have linear : dot normal (sub force (scale (dot normal force / dot normal normal) normal)) =
      dot normal force - (dot normal force / dot normal normal) * dot normal normal := by
    simp only [dot,sub,scale]
    ring
  rw [linear, div_mul_cancel₀ _ nonzero, sub_self]

/-- A rejected native inequality retains its actual clearance, rather than
being silently replaced by a zero-clearance tangent condition. -/
theorem rejected_predicate_affine_boundary (normal step : Point) (clearance : ℝ)
    (nonzero : dot normal normal ≠ 0) :
    clearance + dot normal
      (add step (scale ((-clearance-dot normal step)/dot normal normal) normal)) = 0 := by
  have linear : dot normal
      (add step (scale ((-clearance-dot normal step)/dot normal normal) normal)) =
      dot normal step + ((-clearance-dot normal step)/dot normal normal)*dot normal normal := by
    simp only [dot,add,scale]
    ring
  rw [linear, div_mul_cancel₀ _ nonzero]
  ring

/-- The same clearance-preserving contraction on the complete finite native
coordinate register, including every backbone and sidechain generator. -/
theorem finite_coordinate_affine_boundary {n : ℕ} (row step : Fin n → ℝ)
    (clearance : ℝ) (nonzero : (∑ i, row i * row i) ≠ 0) :
    clearance + (∑ i, row i * (step i +
      ((-clearance-(∑ j, row j * step j))/(∑ j, row j * row j))*row i)) = 0 := by
  let delta := (-clearance-(∑ j, row j * step j))/(∑ j, row j * row j)
  have linear : (∑ i, row i * (step i + delta*row i)) =
      (∑ i, row i*step i) + delta*(∑ i, row i*row i) := by
    rw [Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro i _
    ring
  change clearance + (∑ i, row i * (step i + delta*row i)) = 0
  rw [linear]
  dsimp [delta]
  rw [div_mul_cancel₀ _ nonzero]
  ring

/-! A criterion for discarding distinctions in a carried ensemble.

`State` denotes the whole bounded ensemble, including its correlated alternatives,
not an isolated constituent. `step` must act on that same ensemble. The observation
type retains the required folding, coherence, work and enabled-action readouts.
The results quantify over every finite continuation of the supplied machine.
They do not assert that a particular machine already characterizes protein folding.
-/
namespace Imscribing.Biochem.FoldingDistinctions

universe u v w z

/-- A repeated two-state future can be skipped only with its terminal parity.
The two states are not identified, and a cycle is not declared a fixed point. -/
theorem two_step_return {State : Type u} (step : State → State) (s : State)
    (cycle : step (step s) = s) (k : ℕ) : (step^[2*k]) s = s := by
  induction k with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih =>
    rw [Nat.mul_succ, Function.iterate_add_apply]
    have closed : (step^[2]) s = s := by
      simpa only [Function.iterate_succ_apply, Function.iterate_zero_apply] using cycle
    rw [closed, ih]

theorem two_step_odd_return {State : Type u} (step : State → State) (s : State)
    (cycle : step (step s) = s) (k : ℕ) : (step^[2*k+1]) s = step s := by
  rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', two_step_return step s cycle k]

#print axioms two_step_return
#print axioms two_step_odd_return

def runFrom {State : Type u} {Action : Type v}
    (step : State → Action → State) : List Action → State → State
  | [], s => s
  | a :: rest, s => runFrom step rest (step s a)

def SameFuture {State : Type u} {Action : Type v} {Observation : Type w}
    (step : State → Action → State) (observe : State → Observation)
    (s t : State) : Prop :=
  ∀ continuation, observe (runFrom step continuation s) = observe (runFrom step continuation t)

theorem sameFuture_now {State : Type u} {Action : Type v} {Observation : Type w}
    {step : State → Action → State} {observe : State → Observation} {s t : State}
    (h : SameFuture step observe s t) : observe s = observe t := h []

theorem sameFuture_step {State : Type u} {Action : Type v} {Observation : Type w}
    {step : State → Action → State} {observe : State → Observation} {s t : State}
    (h : SameFuture step observe s t) (a : Action) :
    SameFuture step observe (step s a) (step t a) := by
  intro rest
  exact h (a :: rest)

/-- An identification is adequate when it preserves the current observations
and remains adequate after every generating action on the carried ensemble. -/
def Adequate {State : Type u} {Action : Type v} {Observation : Type w} {Code : Type z}
    (step : State → Action → State) (observe : State → Observation)
    (encode : State → Code) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃s t⦄, encode s = encode t →
    observe s = observe t ∧ ∀ a, encode (step s a) = encode (step t a)

/-- Sufficiency propagates through arbitrary recursive continuation length. -/
theorem adequate_preserves_every_future
    {State : Type u} {Action : Type v} {Observation : Type w} {Code : Type z}
    {step : State → Action → State} {observe : State → Observation} {encode : State → Code}
    (adequate : Adequate step observe encode) {s t : State} (same : encode s = encode t) :
    SameFuture step observe s t := by
  intro continuation
  induction continuation generalizing s t with
  | nil => exact (adequate same).1
  | cons a rest ih => exact ih ((adequate same).2 a)

/-- A positive witness to a different future prevents any adequate encoding
from erasing that distinction. This is the necessity half of the criterion. -/
theorem different_future_requires_distinction
    {State : Type u} {Action : Type v} {Observation : Type w} {Code : Type z}
    {step : State → Action → State} {observe : State → Observation} {encode : State → Code}
    (adequate : Adequate step observe encode) {s t : State} (continuation : List Action)
    (different : observe (runFrom step continuation s) ≠ observe (runFrom step continuation t)) :
    encode s ≠ encode t := by
  intro same
  exact different (adequate_preserves_every_future adequate same continuation)

/-- Future agreement is the coarsest observation-preserving, successor-stable
identification: every other such identification is contained in it. -/
theorem stable_identification_is_contained_in_sameFuture
    {State : Type u} {Action : Type v} {Observation : Type w}
    {step : State → Action → State} {observe : State → Observation}
    (related : State → State → Prop)
    (stable : ∀ ⦃s t⦄, related s t → observe s = observe t ∧ ∀ a, related (step s a) (step t a))
    {s t : State} (h : related s t) : SameFuture step observe s t := by
  intro continuation
  induction continuation generalizing s t with
  | nil => exact (stable h).1
  | cons a rest ih => exact ih ((stable h).2 a)

namespace NativeBankWitness
open Imscribing.Paraconsistent.IMASM16_3Machine

def truthBank : MachineState := run [.FSPLIT3, .EVALT, .AREV]
def falsityBank : MachineState := run [.FSPLIT3, .EVALF, .AREV]

theorem equal_landing_registers : truthBank.reg = falsityBank.reg := by decide

theorem distinct_fuse_returns :
    (step truthBank .FFUSE3).reg ≠ (step falsityBank .FFUSE3).reg := by decide

theorem landing_register_is_insufficient :
    ¬ Adequate step MachineState.reg MachineState.reg := by
  intro adequate
  have same := (adequate equal_landing_registers).2 Mark16_3.FFUSE3
  exact distinct_fuse_returns same

end NativeBankWitness

namespace NativeReverseBridge

/-- Constant and three nonconstant characters of the four named native lanes.
The constant coordinate retains support cardinality; no lane is discarded. -/
def affine (r : Reg16_3) : Int × Int × Int × Int :=
  let a : Int := if Reg16_3.bigT r then 1 else 0
  let b : Int := if Reg16_3.bigF r then 1 else 0
  let c : Int := if Reg16_3.smallT r then 1 else 0
  let d : Int := if Reg16_3.smallF r then 1 else 0
  (a+b+c+d, a-b+c-d, a+b-c-d, a-b-c+d)

def reverseAffine (p : Int × Int × Int × Int) : Int × Int × Int × Int :=
  (p.1, -p.2.1, p.2.2.1, -p.2.2.2)

theorem affine_retains_every_native_distinction :
    ∀ r s : Reg16_3, affine r = affine s → r = s := by decide

theorem affine_transports_actual_reverse :
    ∀ r : Reg16_3, affine (Reg16_3.invol r) = reverseAffine (affine r) := by decide

/-- The third arm emitted by the source's internal native ternary split.
Its two small lanes are retained together. -/
def smallPair : Reg16_3 := Reg16_3.mk false false true true

theorem smallPair_fixed : Reg16_3.invol smallPair = smallPair := rfl

/-- Any domain action transported from AREV must fix the image of its fixed
register. Extra geometric motion requires additional carried state and a
bridge on that state; a slot label alone does not supply that bridge. -/
theorem transported_reverse_fixes_smallPair {Domain : Type u}
    (realize : Reg16_3 → Domain) (reverse : Domain → Domain)
    (commutes : ∀ r, realize (Reg16_3.invol r) = reverse (realize r)) :
    reverse (realize smallPair) = realize smallPair := by
  simpa only [smallPair_fixed] using (commutes smallPair).symm

theorem no_fixed_free_reverse_bridge {Domain : Type u}
    (realize : Reg16_3 → Domain) (reverse : Domain → Domain)
    (no_fixed_point : ∀ d, reverse d ≠ d) :
    ¬ (∀ r, realize (Reg16_3.invol r) = reverse (realize r)) := by
  intro commutes
  exact no_fixed_point _ (transported_reverse_fixes_smallPair realize reverse commutes)

end NativeReverseBridge

/-! Reduced native one-probe joint response, with the geometric guard retained.
This diagnoses the response model's preference; it is not a protein theorem.
-/
namespace Imscribing.Biochem.JointSurfaceResponse

noncomputable def potential (a b c length distance : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  -(a+b*length/distance+c*length*length/(distance*distance))

theorem retained_work (a b c length boundary distance : ℝ)
    (hb : boundary ≠ 0) (hd : distance ≠ 0) :
    potential a b c length distance - potential a b c length boundary =
      (distance-boundary)/(distance*boundary)*
        (b*length+c*length*length*(distance+boundary)/(distance*boundary)) := by
  unfold potential
  field_simp
  <;> ring

/-- Positive response coefficients select the admitted lower separation.
The full conformation still needs its atom and orientation constraints. -/
theorem source_pair_favors_guard_boundary (a b c length boundary distance : ℝ)
    (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hc : 0 ≤ c) (hl : 0 < length) (hboundary : 0 < boundary)
    (admitted : boundary ≤ distance) :
    potential a b c length boundary ≤ potential a b c length distance := by
  have hd : 0 < distance := lt_of_lt_of_le hboundary admitted
  have gap : 0 ≤ distance-boundary := sub_nonneg.mpr admitted
  have work := retained_work a b c length boundary distance (ne_of_gt hboundary) (ne_of_gt hd)
  have nonnegative : 0 ≤ (distance-boundary)/(distance*boundary)*
      (b*length+c*length*length*(distance+boundary)/(distance*boundary)) := by positivity
  linarith

#print axioms retained_work
#print axioms source_pair_favors_guard_boundary
end Imscribing.Biochem.JointSurfaceResponse

/-! One shared proton in a concrete mixed contact Gram realization.
The donor and acceptor remain coordinates of the containing conformation.
The mechanical potential and executing root map are defined together.
This local model does not assert whole-protein closure or a universal bond law.
-/
namespace Imscribing.Biochem.MixedContactGram

def stiffness (pd pa c : ℝ) : ℝ := pd + pa + 2*c
def weight (pd pa c d a : ℝ) : ℝ := (pd+c)*d + (pa+c)*a
def potential (pd pa c d a x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  pd*(x-d)^2 + pa*(x-a)^2 + 2*c*(x-d)*(x-a)
def forceResidual (pd pa c d a x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  2*(stiffness pd pa c*x - weight pd pa c d a)
noncomputable def root (pd pa c d a : ℝ) : ℝ := weight pd pa c d a / stiffness pd pa c

theorem mixed_stiffness_positive {pd pa c im : ℝ}
    (trace : pd+pa=1) (mixed : c*c+im*im < pd*pa) :
    0 < stiffness pd pa c := by
  have hb : 4*c*c < 1 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (pd-pa),sq_nonneg im]
  have hc : -(1/2:ℝ) < c := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (c+(1/2:ℝ))]
  unfold stiffness
  linarith

theorem root_has_zero_force (pd pa c d a : ℝ) (h : stiffness pd pa c ≠ 0) :
    forceResidual pd pa c d a (root pd pa c d a) = 0 := by
  unfold forceResidual root
  field_simp [h]
  <;> ring

theorem complete_gram_square (pd pa c d a x : ℝ) (h : stiffness pd pa c ≠ 0) :
    potential pd pa c d a x - potential pd pa c d a (root pd pa c d a) =
      stiffness pd pa c * (x-root pd pa c d a)^2 := by
  unfold potential root
  field_simp
  dsimp [stiffness,weight] at *
  nlinarith [h]

theorem root_is_stable_minimum (pd pa c d a x : ℝ) (h : 0 < stiffness pd pa c) :
    potential pd pa c d a (root pd pa c d a) ≤ potential pd pa c d a x := by
  have equality := complete_gram_square pd pa c d a x (ne_of_gt h)
  have nonnegative := mul_nonneg (le_of_lt h) (sq_nonneg (x-root pd pa c d a))
  linarith

theorem root_is_unique_minimum (pd pa c d a x : ℝ) (h : 0 < stiffness pd pa c)
    (same : potential pd pa c d a x = potential pd pa c d a (root pd pa c d a)) :
    x = root pd pa c d a := by
  have equality := complete_gram_square pd pa c d a x (ne_of_gt h)
  have square_zero : (x-root pd pa c d a)^2=0 := by nlinarith
  have difference : x-root pd pa c d a=0 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (x-root pd pa c d a)]
  linarith

/-- Eliminating the shared proton retains a donor/acceptor coupling.
Its rest displacement is zero in this model; chemical and steric guards
must remain in the containing conformation. -/
theorem retained_pair_potential (pd pa c d a : ℝ) (h : stiffness pd pa c ≠ 0) :
    potential pd pa c d a (root pd pa c d a) =
      (pd*pa-c*c)/stiffness pd pa c*(d-a)^2 := by
  unfold potential root weight
  field_simp [h]
  dsimp [stiffness]
  ring

/-! Re-entry of the retained release coordinate into the existing native
two-preference realization. This is an explicit realization of the ensemble
continuation, with both source supports and the banked preference retained.
The quadratic completion determines its force readout at the new boundary. -/
namespace Imscribing.Biochem.NativeEnsembleRelease

noncomputable def center (p n z : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt (n * (p * n + z ^ 2) / (p + n))

theorem center_squared (p n z : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) (hn : 0 < n) :
    center p n z ^ 2 = n * (p * n + z ^ 2) / (p + n) := by
  apply Real.sq_sqrt
  positivity

theorem prepared_center (p n : ℝ) (hp : 0 < p) (hn : 0 < n) :
    center p n n = n := by
  unfold center
  have h : n * (p * n + n ^ 2) / (p + n) = n ^ 2 := by
    field_simp
  rw [h, Real.sqrt_sq (le_of_lt hn)]

/-- Both opposed preferences remain in the same potential. Their current
separation is the completion of the retained accessible and banked strain. -/
theorem complete_joint_potential (p n z r q : ℝ) (hn : n ≠ 0)
    (hq : (p + n) * q ^ 2 = n * (p * n + z ^ 2)) :
    p * r ^ 2 / 2 + n * (r - (p + n) * q / n) ^ 2 / 2 =
      (p + n) * (r - q) ^ 2 / 2 + p ^ 2 * n / 2 + p * z ^ 2 / 2 := by
  field_simp
  linear_combination p * hq

theorem retained_bank_and_accessible (p n z : ℝ) :
    p ^ 2 * n / 2 + p * z ^ 2 / 2 = p * (p * n + z ^ 2) / 2 := by ring

theorem force_changes_with_retained_center (p n r a b : ℝ) :
    (p + n) * (r - a) - (p + n) * (r - b) = (p + n) * (b - a) := by ring

/-- The whole conformation's current distance determines the internal
release target. Bank boundaries restrict this target in execution. -/
theorem joint_release_minimum (p n r q : ℝ) (hn : n ≠ 0) (hk : p + n ≠ 0) :
    (p + n) * (r - q) ^ 2 / 2 + p * (p + n) * q ^ 2 / (2 * n) =
      (p + n) ^ 2 / (2 * n) * (q - r * n / (p + n)) ^ 2 + p * r ^ 2 / 2 := by
  field_simp
  <;> ring

theorem different_release_is_a_necessary_distinction (p n r a b : ℝ)
    (hp : 0 < p) (hn : 0 < n) (different : a ≠ b) :
    (p + n) * (r - a) ≠ (p + n) * (r - b) := by
  intro same
  have h : (p + n) * (b - a) = 0 := by
    rw [← force_changes_with_retained_center p n r a b, same]
    ring
  rcases mul_eq_zero.mp h with zero | zero
  · linarith
  · exact different (by linarith)

/-! One complex coordinate carrier contains the ensemble's spatial,
torsional and release fields. Local ququart reconstructions share one unit
anchor. Their common column recovers each coordinate and hence every
cross-frame coherence of the same whole. -/
namespace Imscribing.Biochem.NativeEnsembleSIC
open Imscribing.Millennium.ZetaSICDualFrame

theorem scalar_pair_recovery (x y : ℝ) :
    (((x : ℂ) + (y : ℂ) * Complex.I).re,
      ((x : ℂ) + (y : ℂ) * Complex.I).im) = (x, y) := by simp

theorem shared_anchor_recovery {n : ℕ} (source returned : Fin (n+1) → ℂ)
    (source_anchor : source 0 = 1) (returned_anchor : returned 0 = 1)
    (common_column : ∀ i, returned i * star (returned 0) = source i * star (source 0)) :
    returned = source := by
  funext i
  simpa [source_anchor, returned_anchor] using common_column i

theorem cross_frame_coherence {n : ℕ} (source returned : Fin (n+1) → ℂ)
    (source_anchor : source 0 = 1) (returned_anchor : returned 0 = 1)
    (common_column : ∀ i, returned i * star (returned 0) = source i * star (source 0)) :
    ∀ i j, returned i * star (returned j) = source i * star (source j) := by
  rw [shared_anchor_recovery source returned source_anchor returned_anchor common_column]
  intro i j
  rfl

theorem frame_coordinate_recovery (c : Fin 16 → ℂ) :
    ququartDualGram.mulVec (ququartGram.mulVec c) = c :=
  ququart_coordinate_reconstruction c

theorem same_population_different_phase :
    Complex.normSq (1 : ℂ) = Complex.normSq Complex.I ∧
      (1 : ℂ).im ≠ Complex.I.im := by norm_num

theorem live_release_conservation (c p z work : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) (hp : 0 < p)
    (admitted : work ≤ c * p * z ^ 2 / 2) :
    c * p * (Real.sqrt (2 * (c * p * z ^ 2 / 2 - work) / (c * p))) ^ 2 / 2 + work =
      c * p * z ^ 2 / 2 := by
  have h : 0 ≤ 2 * (c * p * z ^ 2 / 2 - work) / (c * p) :=
    div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (by norm_num) (sub_nonneg.mpr admitted)) (le_of_lt (mul_pos hc hp))
  rw [Real.sq_sqrt h]
  field_simp [ne_of_gt hc, ne_of_gt hp]
  <;> ring

/-! Native joint potential read by the ensemble's own successor description.
The first coordinate is an observed separation, the second the retained
internal center. Their coefficients are the carried membership extents.
The whole executing conformation supplies all such observations together. -/
namespace Imscribing.Biochem.NativeEnsembleSuccessor

noncomputable section

def potential (c p n r q : ℝ) :=
  c * (p+n) * (r-q)^2 / 2 + c*p*(p+n)*q^2/(2*n)
def radialForce (c p n r q : ℝ) := c*(p+n)*(r-q)
def centerForce (c p n r q : ℝ) := c*(p+n)*((p+n)*q/n-r)

theorem radial_increment (c p n r q h : ℝ) :
    potential c p n (r+h) q - potential c p n r q =
      h*radialForce c p n r q + c*(p+n)*h^2/2 := by
  unfold potential radialForce
  ring

theorem center_increment (c p n r q h : ℝ) (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    potential c p n r (q+h) - potential c p n r q =
      h*centerForce c p n r q + c*(p+n)^2*h^2/(2*n) := by
  unfold potential centerForce
  field_simp
  <;> ring

theorem simultaneous_increment (c p n r q a b : ℝ) (hn : n ≠ 0) :
    potential c p n (r+a) (q+b) - potential c p n r q =
      a*radialForce c p n r q + b*centerForce c p n r q +
      c*(p+n)*(a-b)^2/2 + c*p*(p+n)*b^2/(2*n) := by
  unfold potential radialForce centerForce
  field_simp
  <;> ring

theorem normalized_torsion_direction (force quantum : ℝ) :
    force * (-quantum^2*force) = -(quantum*force)^2 := by ring

theorem projected_release_direction (force extent : ℝ) :
    force * (-extent^2*max force 0) ≤ 0 := by
  by_cases h : 0 ≤ force
  · rw [max_eq_left h]
    have hsq : 0 ≤ (extent*force)^2 := sq_nonneg _
    nlinarith
  · rw [max_eq_right (le_of_lt (lt_of_not_ge h))]
    simp

theorem inclusion_retains_the_added_force (c p n d a b r q : ℝ) :
    radialForce c p n r q + radialForce d a b r q - radialForce c p n r q =
      radialForce d a b r q := by ring

#print axioms center_increment
#print axioms simultaneous_increment

#print axioms inclusion_retains_the_added_force

/-! Two-site orbital rewriting on the retained powerset carrier. The two
spin occupancies come from OrbitalBelnap's FOUR. Rewriting retains every
placement with the same two spin counts. No element identities, chemical
valences or dimensional parameters are supplied. -/
namespace Imscribing.PrimaLogica.NativeOrbitalTransfer
open Lean Imscribing.Paraconsistent Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Orbital

instance : Fintype OrbitalState where
  elems := {.empty, .spinUp, .spinDown, .paired}
  complete := by intro x; cases x <;> simp

def up : OrbitalState → Nat
  | .empty | .spinDown => 0
  | .spinUp | .paired => 1
def down : OrbitalState → Nat
  | .empty | .spinUp => 0
  | .spinDown | .paired => 1
def occupied (x : OrbitalState) := up x + down x
def vacant (x : OrbitalState) := (1 - up x) + (1 - down x)

theorem slot_accounting (x : OrbitalState) : occupied x + vacant x = 2 := by
  cases x <;> decide
theorem capacity (x : OrbitalState) : occupied x ≤ 2 := by
  cases x <;> decide

/-- Creation uses the native pair operation only when its spin slot is free.
An occupied slot has no successor, rather than an idempotent fake addition. -/
def create (x : OrbitalState) (spinUp : Bool) : Option OrbitalState :=
  if (if spinUp then up x else down x) = 0 then
    some (pair x (if spinUp then .spinUp else .spinDown))
  else none

theorem create_adds_one (x y : OrbitalState) (s : Bool)
    (h : create x s = some y) : occupied y = occupied x + 1 := by
  cases x <;> cases s <;>
    simp [create, up, down, pair] at h <;> subst y <;> decide

theorem create_preserves_information (x y : OrbitalState) (s : Bool)
    (h : create x s = some y) : OccupancyLE x y := by
  cases x <;> cases s <;>
    simp [create, up, down, pair] at h <;> subst y <;> decide

theorem create_paired_blocked (s : Bool) : create .paired s = none := by
  cases s <;> rfl

theorem create_opposite_fuses (s : Bool) :
    create (if s then .spinUp else .spinDown) (!s) = some .paired := by
  cases s <;> rfl

theorem create_recovers_split_pair :
    create (depair .paired).1 false = some .paired ∧
    create (depair .paired).2 true = some .paired := by
  constructor <;> rfl

/-! An indexed shell retains the shared orbital placements. Unpaired capacity
is an occupancy readout; it does not assign elemental names to shell inputs. -/
def single : OrbitalState → Nat
  | .spinUp | .spinDown => 1
  | .empty | .paired => 0
def pairedCount : OrbitalState → Nat
  | .paired => 1
  | _ => 0
def emptyCount : OrbitalState → Nat
  | .empty => 1
  | _ => 0

theorem occupied_single_pair (x : OrbitalState) :
    single x + 2 * pairedCount x = occupied x := by
  cases x <;> decide
theorem vacant_single_empty (x : OrbitalState) :
    single x + 2 * emptyCount x = vacant x := by
  cases x <;> decide

def shellOccupied (s : List OrbitalState) : Nat := (s.map occupied).sum
def shellVacant (s : List OrbitalState) : Nat := (s.map vacant).sum
def shellSingle (s : List OrbitalState) : Nat := (s.map single).sum
def shellPaired (s : List OrbitalState) : Nat := (s.map pairedCount).sum
def shellEmpty (s : List OrbitalState) : Nat := (s.map emptyCount).sum

theorem shell_slot_accounting (s : List OrbitalState) :
    shellOccupied s + shellVacant s = 2 * s.length := by
  induction s with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
    simp only [shellOccupied, shellVacant, List.map_cons, List.sum_cons,
      List.length_cons] at *
    have hx := slot_accounting x
    omega

theorem shell_occupied_accounting (s : List OrbitalState) :
    shellSingle s + 2 * shellPaired s = shellOccupied s := by
  induction s with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
    simp only [shellSingle, shellPaired, shellOccupied, List.map_cons,
      List.sum_cons] at *
    have hx := occupied_single_pair x
    omega

theorem shell_vacant_accounting (s : List OrbitalState) :
    shellSingle s + 2 * shellEmpty s = shellVacant s := by
  induction s with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
    simp only [shellSingle, shellEmpty, shellVacant, List.map_cons,
      List.sum_cons] at *
    have hx := vacant_single_empty x
    omega

/-- Unpaired bonding capacity is bounded by both occupied and vacant slots.
The full correlated family remains retained on either side of this readout. -/
theorem shell_single_capacity_bound (s : List OrbitalState) :
    shellSingle s ≤ min (shellOccupied s) (shellVacant s) := by
  have ho := shell_occupied_accounting s
  have hv := shell_vacant_accounting s
  omega

/-! Native mechanical readouts on the full filling family. Information-order
selection retains that entire family. This minimum is an energy observation
for the explicitly summed existing Glut coupling, not a state deletion. -/
def spinGlutDouble (p n : Nat) : Nat := p*n*(p+n)
def shellGlutDouble : List OrbitalState → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | x::xs => spinGlutDouble (up x) (down x) + shellGlutDouble xs +
      (xs.map fun y => spinGlutDouble (up x+up y) (down x+down y)).sum

def fillingStates : Nat → List (List OrbitalState)
  | 0 => [[]]
  | n+1 => (fillingStates n).flatMap fun xs =>
      ([.empty,.spinUp,.spinDown,.paired] : List OrbitalState).map fun x => x::xs

theorem mem_fillingStates (s : List OrbitalState) : s ∈ fillingStates s.length := by
  induction s with
  | nil => simp [fillingStates]
  | cons x xs ih =>
    apply List.mem_flatMap.mpr
    refine ⟨xs, ih, ?_⟩
    apply List.mem_map.mpr
    refine ⟨x, ?_, rfl⟩
    cases x <;> simp

def minimumGlutDouble (k electrons : Nat) : Nat :=
  2*(electrons-k)*(2*k+electrons-3)
def polarized (s : List OrbitalState) : Bool :=
  let u := (s.map up).sum
  let d := (s.map down).sum
  u == 0 || d == 0 || u == s.length || d == s.length

set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in
private theorem filling_readout_certificate :
    ((List.range 5).all fun k => (fillingStates k).all fun s =>
      decide (minimumGlutDouble k (shellOccupied s) ≤ shellGlutDouble s) &&
      (if shellGlutDouble s == minimumGlutDouble k (shellOccupied s) then
        decide (shellSingle s = min (shellOccupied s) (2*k-shellOccupied s)) && polarized s
       else true)) = true := by decide

theorem filling_glut_lower_bound (s : List OrbitalState) (hk : s.length ≤ 4) :
    minimumGlutDouble s.length (shellOccupied s) ≤ shellGlutDouble s := by
  have hc := (List.all_eq_true.mp filling_readout_certificate)
    s.length (List.mem_range.mpr (by omega))
  have hs := (List.all_eq_true.mp hc) s (mem_fillingStates s)
  simp only [Bool.and_eq_true_eq_eq_true_and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at hs
  exact hs.1

theorem minimum_filling_has_maximal_singles (s : List OrbitalState)
    (hk : s.length ≤ 4)
    (he : shellGlutDouble s = minimumGlutDouble s.length (shellOccupied s)) :
    shellSingle s = min (shellOccupied s) (2*s.length-shellOccupied s) ∧
      polarized s = true := by
  have hc := (List.all_eq_true.mp filling_readout_certificate)
    s.length (List.mem_range.mpr (by omega))
  have hs := (List.all_eq_true.mp hc) s (mem_fillingStates s)
  simp [he] at hs
  exact hs

/-- A constructive readout attaining the bound; the reversed spin family
is retained alongside it by fillingStates. -/
def filledReadout (k electrons : Nat) : List OrbitalState :=
  if electrons ≤ k then
    List.replicate electrons .spinUp ++ List.replicate (k-electrons) .empty
  else List.replicate (electrons-k) .paired ++ List.replicate (2*k-electrons) .spinUp

set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in
theorem filling_minimum_attained :
    ((List.range 5).all fun k => (List.range (2*k+1)).all fun e =>
      decide ((filledReadout k e).length = k ∧
        shellOccupied (filledReadout k e) = e ∧
        shellGlutDouble (filledReadout k e) = minimumGlutDouble k e)) = true := by decide

abbrev Joint := OrbitalState × OrbitalState
def allJoints : List Joint :=
  ([.empty,.spinUp,.spinDown,.paired] : List OrbitalState).flatMap fun a =>
    ([.empty,.spinUp,.spinDown,.paired] : List OrbitalState).map fun b => (a,b)
def sector (x : Joint) : Nat × Nat := (up x.1 + up x.2, down x.1 + down x.2)
def alternatives (x : Joint) : Finset Joint :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun y => sector y = sector x
def move (x : Joint) (swapUp swapDown : Bool) : Joint :=
  let a := depair x.1
  let b := depair x.2
  (pair (if swapUp then b.1 else a.1) (if swapDown then b.2 else a.2),
   pair (if swapUp then a.1 else b.1) (if swapDown then a.2 else b.2))
def nativeMoves (x : Joint) : Finset Joint :=
  {move x false false, move x false true, move x true false, move x true true}

/-- Split both orbitals, exchange either spin component, and fuse. These
four native operations generate exactly the conserved family. -/
theorem native_moves_complete (x : Joint) : nativeMoves x = alternatives x := by
  rcases x with ⟨a,b⟩
  cases a <;> cases b <;> decide

def close (K : Finset Joint) : Finset Joint := K.biUnion alternatives

@[simp] theorem mem_alternatives (x y : Joint) :
    y ∈ alternatives x ↔ sector y = sector x := by simp [alternatives]

theorem conservation (x y : Joint) (h : y ∈ alternatives x) :
    up y.1 + up y.2 = up x.1 + up x.2 ∧
    down y.1 + down y.2 = down x.1 + down x.2 := by
  have e := (mem_alternatives x y).mp h
  exact ⟨congrArg Prod.fst e, congrArg Prod.snd e⟩

theorem extensive (K : Finset Joint) : K ⊆ close K := by
  intro x hx
  exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨x, hx, by simp⟩

theorem monotone {K L : Finset Joint} (h : K ⊆ L) : close K ⊆ close L := by
  intro y hy
  obtain ⟨x,hx,hyx⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp hy
  exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨x,h hx,hyx⟩

theorem idempotent (K : Finset Joint) : close (close K) = close K := by
  apply Finset.Subset.antisymm
  · intro y hy
    obtain ⟨z,hz,hyz⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp hy
    obtain ⟨x,hx,hzx⟩ := Finset.mem_biUnion.mp hz
    exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨x,hx,
      (mem_alternatives x y).mpr (((mem_alternatives z y).mp hyz).trans
        ((mem_alternatives x z).mp hzx))⟩
  · exact extensive (close K)

/-- The retained family is the inclusion maximum of all admitted rewrites. -/
theorem maximum (K L : Finset Joint)
    (h : ∀ y ∈ L, ∃ x ∈ K, y ∈ alternatives x) : L ⊆ close K := by
  intro y hy
  obtain ⟨x,hx,hyx⟩ := h y hy
  exact Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨x,hx,hyx⟩

def contains (s : Sixteen3) : Belnap → Bool
  | .N => s.hasN | .T => s.hasT | .F => s.hasF | .B => s.hasB
def orbitalUp (s : Sixteen3) : Nat :=
  ([.empty,.spinUp,.spinDown,.paired] : List OrbitalState).foldl
    (fun n x => n + if contains s (orbToB4 x) then up x else 0) 0
def orbitalDown (s : Sixteen3) : Nat :=
  ([.empty,.spinUp,.spinDown,.paired] : List OrbitalState).foldl
    (fun n x => n + if contains s (orbToB4 x) then down x else 0) 0

theorem glut_positive_is_orbital_support (s : Sixteen3) :
    MechanicalGlut.NativeGlut.positive s = orbitalUp s := by
  rcases s with ⟨n,t,f,b⟩
  cases n <;> cases t <;> cases f <;> cases b <;> decide
theorem glut_negative_is_orbital_support (s : Sixteen3) :
    MechanicalGlut.NativeGlut.negative s = orbitalDown s := by
  rcases s with ⟨n,t,f,b⟩
  cases n <;> cases t <;> cases f <;> cases b <;> decide
def source (s t : Sixteen3) : Finset Joint :=
  Finset.univ.filter fun x => contains s (orbToB4 x.1) && contains t (orbToB4 x.2)
def family (s t : Sixteen3) : Finset Joint := close (source s t)
def marginal (K : Finset Joint) : Sixteen3 := Sixteen3.ofBelnap
  (allJoints.any fun x => decide (x ∈ K) && (orbToB4 x.1 == .N || orbToB4 x.2 == .N))
  (allJoints.any fun x => decide (x ∈ K) && (orbToB4 x.1 == .T || orbToB4 x.2 == .T))
  (allJoints.any fun x => decide (x ∈ K) && (orbToB4 x.1 == .F || orbToB4 x.2 == .F))
  (allJoints.any fun x => decide (x ∈ K) && (orbToB4 x.1 == .B || orbToB4 x.2 == .B))
def selected (s t : Sixteen3) : Sixteen3 :=
  Sixteen3.join_i (Sixteen3.join_i s t) (marginal (family s t))

theorem opposed_spins_retained :
    alternatives (.spinUp,.spinDown) =
      {(.spinUp,.spinDown),(.spinDown,.spinUp),(.paired,.empty),(.empty,.paired)} := by
  decide
theorem double_pair_excluded :
    (.paired,.paired) ∉ alternatives (.spinUp,.spinDown) := by decide

/-- The same Glut polynomial acts at each carried spatial channel. Both
coefficients are the conserved source-addressed spin counts. -/
theorem spatial_glut_decomposition (p n q : ℝ) :
    (p*q^2+n*(q-(p+n))^2)/2 =
      (p+n)*(q-n)^2/2+p*n*(p+n)/2 := by ring
theorem spatial_glut_force (p n q : ℝ) :
    p*q+n*(q-(p+n)) = (p+n)*(q-n) := by ring
theorem transfer_preserves_spatial_coefficients (x y : Joint)
    (h : y ∈ alternatives x) :
    up y.1 + up y.2 = up x.1 + up x.2 ∧
    down y.1 + down y.2 = down x.1 + down x.2 := conservation x y h

/-- Splitting held energy into coordinate deformation and the banked Glut
release coordinate agrees with the original plant on its prepared slice. -/
noncomputable def releasedLift (p n q z : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (p+n)*(q-n)^2/2+p*z^2/2+n*(n-(p+n))^2/2
theorem prepared_release_lift (p n q : ℝ) :
    releasedLift p n q n = (p*q^2+n*(q-(p+n))^2)/2 := by
  unfold releasedLift
  ring
theorem released_lift_exchange (p n qb qa zb za : ℝ)
    (h : (p+n)*(qa-n)^2/2-(p+n)*(qb-n)^2/2 = p*(zb^2-za^2)/2) :
    releasedLift p n qa za = releasedLift p n qb zb := by
  unfold releasedLift
  linear_combination h

abbrev Plant := MechanicalGlut.MechanicalGlut
abbrev Release (m : Plant) (Allowed : Plant → Prop) :=
  MechanicalGlut.MechanicalGlut.ProductiveRelease m Allowed

/-- Coupling efficiency is obtained from measured output work and checked
against the source release budget; it is not supplied as a fitted value. -/
noncomputable def measuredRelease (m : Plant) {Allowed : Plant → Prop}
    (admissible : Allowed m) (work : ℝ) (hw : 0 < work) (hle : work ≤ m.Eg) :
    Release m Allowed where
  admissible := admissible
  eta := work/m.Eg
  eta_pos := div_pos hw m.Eg_pos
  eta_le_one := (div_le_one m.Eg_pos).mpr hle

theorem measured_release_work (m : Plant) {Allowed : Plant → Prop}
    (admissible : Allowed m) (work : ℝ) (hw : 0 < work) (hle : work ≤ m.Eg) :
    m.Wext (measuredRelease m admissible work hw hle) = work := by
  simp only [MechanicalGlut.MechanicalGlut.Wext, measuredRelease]
  exact div_mul_cancel₀ work (ne_of_gt m.Eg_pos)

def jointIndex (x : Joint) : Nat :=
  4 * belnapToNat (orbToB4 x.1) + belnapToNat (orbToB4 x.2)
def jointMask (K : Finset Joint) : Nat :=
  allJoints.foldl (fun mask x => if x ∈ K then mask + 2 ^ jointIndex x else mask) 0
def nativeMask (s : Sixteen3) : Nat :=
  s.hasN.toNat + 2*s.hasT.toNat + 4*s.hasF.toNat + 8*s.hasB.toNat

/-! Exact joint-interaction closure for an ordered pair of native SIXTEEN_3
residue states, with the coefficient address carried through FOUR's character
frame. -/
namespace Imscribing.PrimaLogica.MechanicalGlut.LatticeInteraction

open Lean Imscribing.Paraconsistent

abbrev PairResponse := Sixteen3 → Sixteen3 → ℝ

/-- Apply the native four-membership Möbius operator to the left residue. -/
noncomputable def interactLeft (f : PairResponse) : PairResponse :=
  fun s t => interactions (fun s' => f s' t) s

/-- Apply the native four-membership Möbius operator to the right residue. -/
noncomputable def interactRight (f : PairResponse) : PairResponse :=
  fun s t => interactions (fun t' => f s t') t

/-- The full 256-state residue-pair interaction decomposition: eight
membership differences, four at each source-addressed residue. -/
noncomputable def pairInteractions (f : PairResponse) : PairResponse :=
  interactRight (interactLeft f)

noncomputable def reconstructLeft (f : PairResponse) : PairResponse :=
  fun s t => reconstruct (fun s' => f s' t) s

noncomputable def reconstructRight (f : PairResponse) : PairResponse :=
  fun s t => reconstruct (fun t' => f s t') t

/-- Rebuild the pair response from its eight-difference coefficients. -/
noncomputable def reconstructPair (f : PairResponse) : PairResponse :=
  reconstructLeft (reconstructRight f)

theorem reconstructPair_pairInteractions (f : PairResponse) :
    reconstructPair (pairInteractions f) = f := by
  funext s t
  simp [reconstructPair, pairInteractions, reconstructLeft, reconstructRight,
    interactLeft, interactRight, reconstruct_interactions]

theorem pairInteractions_reconstructPair (f : PairResponse) :
    pairInteractions (reconstructPair f) = f := by
  funext s t
  simp [reconstructPair, pairInteractions, reconstructLeft, reconstructRight,
    interactLeft, interactRight, interactions_reconstruct]

/-- The affine tetrahedral address of one full support subset. Cardinality
retains the constant character while the three coordinates retain FOUR's
nontrivial characters. -/
def supportFrameAddress (s : Sixteen3) : ℕ × (ℚ × ℚ × ℚ) :=
  (s.hasN.toNat + s.hasT.toNat + s.hasF.toNat + s.hasB.toNat,
   (if s.hasN then NativeFrame.vertex .N else (0,0,0)) +
   (if s.hasT then NativeFrame.vertex .T else (0,0,0)) +
   (if s.hasF then NativeFrame.vertex .F else (0,0,0)) +
   (if s.hasB then NativeFrame.vertex .B else (0,0,0)))

/-- The affine tetrahedral address distinguishes all sixteen support subsets,
including the empty and complete supports whose vertex sums both vanish. -/
theorem supportFrameAddress_injective : Function.Injective supportFrameAddress := by
  intro s t h
  rcases s with ⟨sn,st,sf,sb⟩
  rcases t with ⟨tn,tt,tf,tb⟩
  simp only [supportFrameAddress, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
  rcases h with ⟨hc,hv⟩
  cases sn <;> cases st <;> cases sf <;> cases sb <;>
    cases tn <;> cases tt <;> cases tf <;> cases tb
  all_goals simp_all [NativeFrame.vertex, NativeFrame.truthCharacter,
    NativeFrame.falseCharacter, Imscribing.Paraconsistent.designated,
    Imscribing.Paraconsistent.bnot]
  all_goals norm_num at *

/-- A pair coefficient address is retained by the product of the two affine
tetrahedral support addresses. -/
def pairFrameAddress (s t : Sixteen3) :
    (ℕ × (ℚ × ℚ × ℚ)) × (ℕ × (ℚ × ℚ × ℚ)) :=
  (supportFrameAddress s, supportFrameAddress t)

theorem pairFrameAddress_injective {s₁ t₁ s₂ t₂ : Sixteen3}
    (h : pairFrameAddress s₁ t₁ = pairFrameAddress s₂ t₂) :
    s₁ = s₂ ∧ t₁ = t₂ := by
  simp only [pairFrameAddress, Prod.mk.injEq] at h
  exact ⟨supportFrameAddress_injective h.1, supportFrameAddress_injective h.2⟩

/-- Contract one lattice join/meet pair in the affine FOUR frame. The
constant character (support cardinality) wedges with the three tetrahedral
characters, so no character coordinate is silently discarded. -/
def affineFrameWedge (a b : Sixteen3) : ℚ × ℚ × ℚ :=
  let (ra, pa) := supportFrameAddress a
  let (rb, pb) := supportFrameAddress b
  ((ra : ℚ) * pb.1 - (rb : ℚ) * pa.1,
   (ra : ℚ) * pb.2.1 - (rb : ℚ) * pa.2.1,
   (ra : ℚ) * pb.2.2 - (rb : ℚ) * pa.2.2)

def addFrameVectors (a b : ℚ × ℚ × ℚ) : ℚ × ℚ × ℚ :=
  (a.1 + b.1, a.2.1 + b.2.1, a.2.2 + b.2.2)

/-- The one pair contraction retains all three native SIXTEEN₃ orders:
information, truth, and falsity, each as its join/meet boundary in FOUR's
affine character frame. -/
def pairContextContraction (s t : Sixteen3) : ℚ × ℚ × ℚ :=
  addFrameVectors
    (addFrameVectors
      (affineFrameWedge (Sixteen3.join_i s t) (Sixteen3.meet_i s t))
      (affineFrameWedge (Sixteen3.join_t s t) (Sixteen3.meet_t s t)))
    (affineFrameWedge (Sixteen3.join_f s t) (Sixteen3.meet_f s t))

/-- Native pair radial target from the sum of the two residue support
quadratics. It is exactly the inverse-stiffness one-step value first/k. -/
noncomputable def pairRadialTarget (s t : Sixteen3) : ℝ :=
  let ps : ℝ := NativeGlut.positive s
  let ns : ℝ := NativeGlut.negative s
  let pt : ℝ := NativeGlut.positive t
  let nt : ℝ := NativeGlut.negative t
  let k := ps + ns + pt + nt
  let first := ns * (ps + ns) + nt * (pt + nt)
  if hk : k = 0 then 0 else first / k

/-! ### Whole-chain composition

The pair contraction composes by tensor incidence over every unordered
residue pair. Each residue accumulates the stiffness and first moment of its
incident pair terms; the single chain contraction is the corresponding
source-derived affine minimizer. No pair output is fed serially into the
next pair, so the result is independent of pair enumeration. -/

abbrev Peptide20 := Fin 20 → Sixteen3
abbrev Backbone20 := Fin 20 → ℝ

noncomputable def pairStiffness (s t : Sixteen3) : ℝ :=
  (NativeGlut.positive s : ℝ) + NativeGlut.negative s +
    NativeGlut.positive t + NativeGlut.negative t

noncomputable def pairFirstMoment (s t : Sixteen3) : ℝ :=
  (NativeGlut.negative s : ℝ) *
      (NativeGlut.positive s + NativeGlut.negative s) +
    NativeGlut.negative t *
      (NativeGlut.positive t + NativeGlut.negative t)

/-- Tensor the pair quadratics across the complete chain, retaining each
pair through its incidence at a residue. -/
noncomputable def chainStiffness (source : Peptide20) (i : Fin 20) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, pairStiffness (source i) (source j)

noncomputable def chainFirstMoment (source : Peptide20) (i : Fin 20) : ℝ :=
  ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, pairFirstMoment (source i) (source j)

/-- One simultaneous contraction of all 190 pair terms. The incoming
backbone is contracted once against the full source-derived chain tensor. -/
noncomputable def wholeChainContraction (source : Peptide20)
    (backbone : Backbone20) : Backbone20 := fun i =>
  let k := chainStiffness source i
  let first := chainFirstMoment source i
  if hk : k = 0 then backbone i else first / k

theorem wholeChainContraction_fixed (source : Peptide20)
    (backbone : Backbone20) :
    wholeChainContraction source (wholeChainContraction source backbone) =
      wholeChainContraction source backbone := by
  funext i
  simp only [wholeChainContraction]
  split
  · rfl
  · rename_i hk
    simp [hk]

/-- Apply that pair contraction once to the complete reconstructed joint
distribution. `pairInteractions` supplies the signed eight-difference
coefficients; `reconstructPair` restores every source state before the
single character-frame contraction. -/
noncomputable def oneShotPairContraction (coefficients : PairResponse) :
    ℝ × ℝ × ℝ :=
  Finset.univ.sum fun si : Fin 16 =>
    Finset.univ.sum fun ti : Fin 16 =>
      let s := Sixteen3.ofMask si.val
      let t := Sixteen3.ofMask ti.val
      let mass := reconstructPair coefficients s t
      let frame := pairContextContraction s t
      let radial := pairRadialTarget s t
      (mass * radial * (frame.1 : ℝ), mass * radial * (frame.2.1 : ℝ),
       mass * radial * (frame.2.2 : ℝ))

/-- Exact signed shell-channel contraction. The incidence weight records
which containing support families admit the addressed shell channel. -/
noncomputable def shellPushforward (weight : Fin 256 → Fin 16 → ℤ)
    (coefficients : Fin 256 → ℤ) (channel : Fin 16) : ℤ :=
  ∑ support, coefficients support * weight support channel

theorem shellPushforward_add (weight : Fin 256 → Fin 16 → ℤ)
    (a b : Fin 256 → ℤ) (channel : Fin 16) :
    shellPushforward weight (fun k => a k + b k) channel =
      shellPushforward weight a channel + shellPushforward weight b channel := by
  simp [shellPushforward, add_mul, Finset.sum_add_distrib]

/-- Grouping retained interaction shells cannot change the returned channel. -/
theorem shellPushforward_associative (weight : Fin 256 → Fin 16 → ℤ)
    (a b c : Fin 256 → ℤ) (channel : Fin 16) :
    shellPushforward weight (fun k => (a k + b k) + c k) channel =
      shellPushforward weight (fun k => a k + (b k + c k)) channel := by
  simp only [add_assoc]

/-- Move a spatial response through the incidence reconstruction without
collapsing its joint-state addresses to shell-channel marginals. The response
may depend on the full carried conformation. -/
theorem jointResponse_incidence_dual (incidence : Fin 256 → Fin 256 → ℝ)
    (coefficients response : Fin 256 → ℝ) :
    (∑ state, (∑ support, coefficients support * incidence support state) * response state) =
      ∑ support, coefficients support * (∑ state, incidence support state * response state) := by
  simp_rw [Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum, mul_assoc]
  exact Finset.sum_comm

/-- Rational half-angle action on the plane normal to a retained bond.
The parameter is algebraic; no angle or trigonometric evaluation is needed. -/
noncomputable def rotationCos (t : ℝ) : ℝ := (1-t*t)/(1+t*t)
noncomputable def rotationSin (t : ℝ) : ℝ := (2*t)/(1+t*t)

theorem rational_rotation_unit (t : ℝ) :
    rotationCos t ^ 2 + rotationSin t ^ 2 = 1 := by
  have h : (1+t*t : ℝ) ≠ 0 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg t]
  unfold rotationCos rotationSin
  field_simp
  <;> ring

theorem rational_rotation_preserves_norm (t x y : ℝ) :
    (rotationCos t*x-rotationSin t*y)^2 +
      (rotationSin t*x+rotationCos t*y)^2 = x^2+y^2 := by
  have h := rational_rotation_unit t
  calc
    _ = (rotationCos t^2+rotationSin t^2)*(x^2+y^2) := by ring
    _ = x^2+y^2 := by rw [h]; ring

/-- Total extension of the native support quadratic, including zero extents.
Its physical displacement interpretation remains an explicit model input. -/
noncomputable def sourceSupportPotential (s : Sixteen3) (q : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  let p : ℝ := NativeGlut.positive s
  let n : ℝ := NativeGlut.negative s
  p*q^2/2+n*(q-(p+n))^2/2

theorem sourceSupportPotential_moments (s : Sixteen3) (q : ℝ) :
    sourceSupportPotential s q =
      (((NativeGlut.positive s : ℝ)+NativeGlut.negative s)*q^2 -
       2*(NativeGlut.negative s : ℝ)*(NativeGlut.positive s+NativeGlut.negative s)*q +
       (NativeGlut.negative s : ℝ)*(NativeGlut.positive s+NativeGlut.negative s)^2)/2 := by
  unfold sourceSupportPotential
  push_cast
  ring

theorem sourceSupportPotential_derivative (s : Sixteen3) (q : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (sourceSupportPotential s)
      (((NativeGlut.positive s : ℝ)+NativeGlut.negative s)*q -
       (NativeGlut.negative s : ℝ)*(NativeGlut.positive s+NativeGlut.negative s)) q := by
  unfold sourceSupportPotential
  convert (((hasDerivAt_id q).pow 2).const_mul (NativeGlut.positive s : ℝ)).div_const 2 |>.add
    (((((hasDerivAt_id q).sub_const ((NativeGlut.positive s : ℝ)+NativeGlut.negative s)).pow 2).const_mul
      (NativeGlut.negative s : ℝ)).div_const 2) using 1 <;> simp only [id_eq] <;> push_cast <;> ring

/-- Native affine mechanical action at its inverse-stiffness step. -/
noncomputable def radialNest (k first q : ℝ) : ℝ := q-(k*q-first)/k

theorem radialNest_one_shot (k first q : ℝ) (hk : k ≠ 0) :
    radialNest k first q = first/k := by
  unfold radialNest
  field_simp
  <;> ring

theorem radialNest_idempotent (k first q : ℝ) (hk : k ≠ 0) :
    radialNest k first (radialNest k first q) = radialNest k first q := by
  rw [radialNest_one_shot k first _ hk, radialNest_one_shot k first _ hk]

/-- A source character winding supplies an algebraic unit direction directly.
The positive square root selects the source's oriented branch; an angle is
unnecessary for the backbone construction. -/
theorem sourceWinding_direction_unit (x y radius : ℝ)
    (hr : radius ≠ 0) (hs : radius^2 = x^2+y^2) :
    (x/radius)^2+(y/radius)^2 = 1 := by
  field_simp
  nlinarith

theorem sourceWinding_direction_pairing (x y radius : ℝ)
    (hr : radius ≠ 0) :
    (x/radius)*y = (y/radius)*x := by
  field_simp
  <;> ring

/-- Channel deformation plus the retained bank expressed in preference q.
The common source multiplicity can multiply this whole expression. -/
noncomputable def conditionalBankEnergy (p n d q : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (p+n)*(d-q)^2/2+p*((p+n)*q^2/n-p*n)/2

theorem conditionalBank_completed_square (p n d q : ℝ)
    (hn : n ≠ 0) (hs : p+n ≠ 0) :
    conditionalBankEnergy p n d q - conditionalBankEnergy p n d (n*d/(p+n)) =
      (p+n)^2/(2*n)*(q-n*d/(p+n))^2 := by
  unfold conditionalBankEnergy
  field_simp
  <;> ring

theorem conditionalBank_minimum (p n d q : ℝ)
    (hn : 0 < n) (hs : p+n ≠ 0) :
    conditionalBankEnergy p n d (n*d/(p+n)) ≤ conditionalBankEnergy p n d q := by
  have h := conditionalBank_completed_square p n d q (ne_of_gt hn) hs
  have hc : 0 ≤ (p+n)^2/(2*n) := div_nonneg (sq_nonneg _) (by positivity)
  have hr := mul_nonneg hc (sq_nonneg (q-n*d/(p+n)))
  linarith

noncomputable def retainedClamp (lower upper x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  max lower (min upper x)

theorem retainedClamp_idempotent (lower upper x : ℝ) (h : lower ≤ upper) :
    retainedClamp lower upper (retainedClamp lower upper x) = retainedClamp lower upper x := by
  have hl : lower ≤ retainedClamp lower upper x := le_max_left _ _
  have hu : retainedClamp lower upper x ≤ upper := max_le h (min_le_left _ _)
  change max lower (min upper (retainedClamp lower upper x)) = retainedClamp lower upper x
  rw [min_eq_right hu, max_eq_right hl]

theorem retainedClamp_distance (lower upper x q : ℝ)
    (hlu : lower ≤ upper) (hlq : lower ≤ q) (hqu : q ≤ upper) :
    (retainedClamp lower upper x-x)^2 ≤ (q-x)^2 := by
  by_cases hxl : x ≤ lower
  · have hc : retainedClamp lower upper x = lower := by
      simp [retainedClamp, min_eq_right (le_trans hxl hlu), max_eq_left hxl]
    rw [hc]
    nlinarith [mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hlq) (show 0 ≤ q+lower-2*x by linarith)]
  · by_cases hux : upper ≤ x
    · have hc : retainedClamp lower upper x = upper := by
        simp [retainedClamp, min_eq_left hux, max_eq_right hlu]
      rw [hc]
      nlinarith [mul_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr hqu) (show 0 ≤ 2*x-q-upper by linarith)]
    · have hc : retainedClamp lower upper x = x := by
        simp [retainedClamp, min_eq_right (le_of_not_ge hux),
          max_eq_right (le_of_not_ge hxl)]
      rw [hc]
      simpa using sq_nonneg (q-x)

theorem conditionalBank_constrained_minimum (p n d lower upper q : ℝ)
    (hn : 0 < n) (hs : p+n ≠ 0) (hlu : lower ≤ upper)
    (hlq : lower ≤ q) (hqu : q ≤ upper) :
    conditionalBankEnergy p n d (retainedClamp lower upper (n*d/(p+n))) ≤
      conditionalBankEnergy p n d q := by
  have ha := conditionalBank_completed_square p n d
    (retainedClamp lower upper (n*d/(p+n))) (ne_of_gt hn) hs
  have hb := conditionalBank_completed_square p n d q (ne_of_gt hn) hs
  have hd := retainedClamp_distance lower upper (n*d/(p+n)) q hlu hlq hqu
  have hc : 0 ≤ (p+n)^2/(2*n) := div_nonneg (sq_nonneg _) (by positivity)
  have hm := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hd hc
  linarith

end Imscribing.PrimaLogica.MechanicalGlut.LatticeInteraction

/-! Exact composition of the existing native Glut readout on indexed shells.
The source remains a list of FOUR occupancies. Counts are additive observers;
they do not replace the retained placements or select a filling branch. -/
namespace Imscribing.PrimaLogica.NativeOrbitalTransfer
open Imscribing.Paraconsistent.Orbital

def shellUp (s : List OrbitalState) : Nat := (s.map up).sum
def shellDown (s : List OrbitalState) : Nat := (s.map down).sum

theorem pair_glut_composition (a b : OrbitalState) :
    spinGlutDouble (up a + up b) (down a + down b) =
      2 * (up a * down b + up b * down a +
        pairedCount a * (1 + up b + down b) +
        pairedCount b * (1 + up a + down a)) := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> decide

theorem single_glut (a : OrbitalState) :
    spinGlutDouble (up a) (down a) = 2 * pairedCount a := by
  cases a <;> decide

theorem pair_glut_sum (a : OrbitalState) (s : List OrbitalState) :
    (s.map fun b => spinGlutDouble (up a + up b) (down a + down b)).sum =
      2 * (up a * shellDown s + down a * shellUp s +
        pairedCount a * (s.length + shellUp s + shellDown s) +
        shellPaired s * (1 + up a + down a)) := by
  induction s with
  | nil => simp [shellUp, shellDown, shellPaired]
  | cons b s ih =>
    simp only [List.map_cons, List.sum_cons, List.length_cons, pair_glut_composition,
      shellUp, shellDown, shellPaired] at *
    rw [ih]
    ring

/-- A subtraction-free whole-shell identity, valid at every shell size. -/
theorem shell_glut_closed (s : List OrbitalState) :
    shellGlutDouble s + 6 * shellPaired s =
      2 * shellUp s * shellDown s +
        2 * shellPaired s * (s.length + shellUp s + shellDown s) := by
  induction s with
  | nil => simp [shellGlutDouble, shellUp, shellDown, shellPaired]
  | cons a s ih =>
    rw [shellGlutDouble, single_glut, pair_glut_sum]
    cases a <;>
      simp only [shellUp, shellDown, shellPaired, List.map_cons, List.sum_cons,
        List.length_cons, up, down, pairedCount] at * <;> nlinarith

/-- Full fusion adds each cross-shell pair once, retaining the two source
shells and their internal Glut. No valence or interaction coefficient is input. -/
theorem shell_glut_fusion (a b : List OrbitalState) :
    shellGlutDouble (a ++ b) = shellGlutDouble a + shellGlutDouble b +
      2 * (shellUp a * shellDown b + shellUp b * shellDown a +
        shellPaired a * (b.length + shellUp b + shellDown b) +
        shellPaired b * (a.length + shellUp a + shellDown a)) := by
  have ha := shell_glut_closed a
  have hb := shell_glut_closed b
  have hab := shell_glut_closed (a ++ b)
  simp only [shellUp, shellDown, shellPaired, List.map_append, List.sum_append,
    List.length_append] at *
  nlinarith

theorem shell_glut_fusion_associative (a b c : List OrbitalState) :
    shellGlutDouble ((a ++ b) ++ c) = shellGlutDouble (a ++ (b ++ c)) := by
  rw [List.append_assoc]

#print axioms shell_glut_closed
#print axioms shell_glut_fusion
#print axioms shell_glut_fusion_associative

/-! Inventory and frame identities for the unfused terminal carboxyl port.
These establish the open-chain count and the chosen source-frame lift.
They do not determine an absolute bond length or a native fold. -/
namespace Imscribing.Biochem.OpenCarboxylBoundary

theorem retained_oxygen_count (n : ℕ) (nonempty : 0 < n) :
    2*n-(n-1)=n+1 := by omega

abbrev Point := ℝ × ℝ × ℝ
def dot (x y : Point) := x.1*y.1+x.2.1*y.2.1+x.2.2*y.2.2
def halfTurn (a x : Point) : Point :=
  (2*dot a x*a.1-x.1, 2*dot a x*a.2.1-x.2.1,
   2*dot a x*a.2.2-x.2.2)

theorem axial_projection (a x : Point) (unit : dot a a=1) :
    dot a (halfTurn a x)=dot a x := by
  have h : dot a (halfTurn a x) = 2*dot a x*dot a a-dot a x := by
    simp only [dot,halfTurn]; ring
  rw [h,unit]; ring

theorem squared_length (a x : Point) (unit : dot a a=1) :
    dot (halfTurn a x) (halfTurn a x)=dot x x := by
  have h : dot (halfTurn a x) (halfTurn a x) =
      dot x x+4*(dot a x)^2*(dot a a-1) := by
    simp only [dot,halfTurn]; ring
  rw [h,unit]; ring

/-! The coordinate coefficient generated by source contact commutators is a
distance polarization. Four noncoplanar anchor observations determine a point.
The anchor hypothesis is explicit; singular configurations remain open.
-/
namespace Imscribing.Biochem.PeptideCoordinateBridge

abbrev Point := ℝ × ℝ × ℝ
def sub (a b : Point) : Point := (a.1-b.1,a.2.1-b.2.1,a.2.2-b.2.2)
def dot (a b : Point) : ℝ := a.1*b.1+a.2.1*b.2.1+a.2.2*b.2.2
def distanceSq (a b : Point) : ℝ := dot (sub a b) (sub a b)
def coefficient (a b c : Point) : ℝ := 2*dot (sub b c) (sub b a)
def combination (r s t : ℝ) (a b c : Point) : Point :=
  (r*a.1+s*b.1+t*c.1,r*a.2.1+s*b.2.1+t*c.2.1,r*a.2.2+s*b.2.2+t*c.2.2)

theorem contact_polarization (a b c : Point) :
    coefficient a b c = distanceSq a b + distanceSq b c - distanceSq a c := by
  simp only [coefficient,distanceSq,dot,sub]
  ring

theorem loop_distance (a b : Point) : coefficient a b a / 2 = distanceSq a b := by
  simp only [coefficient,distanceSq,dot,sub]
  ring

theorem recover_distance (a b c : Point) :
    distanceSq a c = coefficient a b a / 2 + coefficient b c b / 2 - coefficient a b c := by
  rw [loop_distance,loop_distance,contact_polarization]
  ring

theorem anchor_orthogonality {x y a b : Point}
    (ha : distanceSq x a = distanceSq y a)
    (hb : distanceSq x b = distanceSq y b) : dot (sub x y) (sub b a) = 0 := by
  simp only [distanceSq,dot,sub] at ha hb ⊢
  nlinarith [ha,hb]

theorem four_anchors_determine_point {x y a b c d : Point}
    (spans : ∀ v : Point, ∃ r s t : ℝ, v = combination r s t (sub b a) (sub c a) (sub d a))
    (ha : distanceSq x a = distanceSq y a)
    (hb : distanceSq x b = distanceSq y b)
    (hc : distanceSq x c = distanceSq y c)
    (hd : distanceSq x d = distanceSq y d) : x = y := by
  have h₁ := anchor_orthogonality ha hb
  have h₂ := anchor_orthogonality ha hc
  have h₃ := anchor_orthogonality ha hd
  obtain ⟨r,s,t,hs⟩ := spans (sub x y)
  have hn : dot (sub x y) (sub x y) = 0 := by
    calc
      dot (sub x y) (sub x y) = dot (sub x y) (combination r s t (sub b a) (sub c a) (sub d a)) := by rw [← hs]
      _ = r*dot (sub x y) (sub b a) + s*dot (sub x y) (sub c a) + t*dot (sub x y) (sub d a) := by
        simp only [dot,combination]; ring
      _ = 0 := by rw [h₁,h₂,h₃]; ring
  simp only [dot,sub] at hn
  have hx : (x.1-y.1)^2 = 0 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (x.2.1-y.2.1),sq_nonneg (x.2.2-y.2.2)]
  have hy : (x.2.1-y.2.1)^2 = 0 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (x.1-y.1),sq_nonneg (x.2.2-y.2.2)]
  have hz : (x.2.2-y.2.2)^2 = 0 := by nlinarith [sq_nonneg (x.1-y.1),sq_nonneg (x.2.1-y.2.1)]
  have ex : x.1-y.1 = 0 := by simpa using hx
  have ey : x.2.1-y.2.1 = 0 := by simpa using hy
  have ez : x.2.2-y.2.2 = 0 := by simpa using hz
  exact Prod.ext (sub_eq_zero.mp ex) (Prod.ext (sub_eq_zero.mp ey) (sub_eq_zero.mp ez))

/-! The supplied peptide word's B sector composes eight copies of the same
carried source relation. Banked re-entry retains the source and that return.
The resulting seven-step congruence is derived from the word, not supplied
as a clock parameter. These are carrier laws, not a folding completion claim.
-/
namespace Imscribing.Biochem.PeptideLatticeReentry

structure Channels (α : Type*) where
  n : α
  t : α
  f : α
  b : α

variable {α : Type*} [Semiring α]

def evalT (x : Channels α) : Channels α := ⟨0, x.t, 0, x.b⟩
def evalF (x : Channels α) : Channels α := ⟨x.n, 0, x.f, 0⟩
def arev (x : Channels α) : Channels α := ⟨x.t, x.n, x.b, x.f⟩
def clink (x : Channels α) : Channels α := ⟨x.n*x.n, x.t*x.t, x.f*x.f, x.b*x.b⟩
def fuse (x y : Channels α) : Channels α := ⟨x.n+y.n, x.t+y.t, x.f+y.f, x.b+y.b⟩
def engage (basis : α) (x : Channels α) : Channels α := ⟨basis, basis, x.f, x.b⟩

/-- Native nodes 3→13, 14→15 and 17→25, with identity/forward nodes omitted.
`basis` is the retained path language at the paradox node. -/
def body (x : Channels α) (basis : α) : Channels α :=
  let t₁ := evalT (clink (evalT x))
  let f₁ := evalF (arev (evalF x))
  let rejoined := engage basis (clink (fuse t₁ f₁))
  let t₂ := clink (evalT rejoined)
  let f₂ := evalF (arev (evalF rejoined))
  fuse t₂ f₂

theorem body_B (x : Channels α) (basis : α) : (body x basis).b = x.b ^ 8 := by
  simp [body, evalT, evalF, arev, clink, fuse, engage, pow_succ, mul_assoc]

theorem body_N (x : Channels α) (basis : α) : (body x basis).n = 0 := by
  simp [body, evalT, evalF, arev, clink, fuse, engage]

theorem body_F (x : Channels α) (basis : α) : (body x basis).f = 0 := by
  simp [body, evalT, evalF, arev, clink, fuse, engage]

inductive BTree where
  | source
  | eight (a b c d e f g h : BTree)

def leaves : BTree → Nat
  | .source => 1
  | .eight a b c d e f g h =>
    leaves a + leaves b + leaves c + leaves d + leaves e + leaves f + leaves g + leaves h

theorem leaves_mod_seven (tree : BTree) : leaves tree % 7 = 1 := by
  induction tree with
  | source => decide
  | eight a b c d e f g h ha hb hc hd he hf hg hh =>
    simp [leaves, Nat.add_mod, ha, hb, hc, hd, he, hf, hg, hh]

def comb : Nat → BTree
  | 0 => .source
  | k+1 => .eight .source .source .source .source .source .source .source (comb k)

theorem leaves_comb (k : Nat) : leaves (comb k) = 1 + 7*k := by
  induction k with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih => simp only [comb, leaves, ih]; omega

theorem exact_clock_language (n : Nat) :
    (∃ tree : BTree, leaves tree = n) ↔ ∃ k : Nat, n = 1 + 7*k := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨tree, rfl⟩
    have h := leaves_mod_seven tree
    refine ⟨leaves tree / 7, ?_⟩
    omega
  · rintro ⟨k, rfl⟩
    exact ⟨comb k, leaves_comb k⟩

#print axioms body_B
#print axioms exact_clock_language

/-! Source paths retain their boundary register and ordered component ancestry.
These are laws of the executing path carrier, not a completed folding theorem.
-/
namespace Imscribing.Biochem.PeptideSourcePaths

abbrev Boundary := Nat × Reg16_3

def reverseBoundary (b : Boundary) : Boundary := (b.1, Reg16_3.invol b.2)

theorem reverseBoundary_twice (b : Boundary) :
    reverseBoundary (reverseBoundary b) = b := by
  cases b
  simp [reverseBoundary, Reg16_3.invol_involutive]

structure SourcePath where
  source : Boundary
  target : Boundary
  steps : List (Nat × Bool)
  deriving DecidableEq

def Composable (p q : SourcePath) : Prop := p.target = q.source

def compose (p q : SourcePath) : SourcePath :=
  ⟨p.source, q.target, p.steps ++ q.steps⟩

def identity (b : Boundary) : SourcePath := ⟨b, b, []⟩

def flipStep (s : Nat × Bool) : Nat × Bool := (s.1, !s.2)

def dagger (p : SourcePath) : SourcePath :=
  ⟨reverseBoundary p.target, reverseBoundary p.source,
   p.steps.reverse.map flipStep⟩

theorem compose_associative (p q r : SourcePath) :
    compose (compose p q) r = compose p (compose q r) := by
  simp [compose, List.append_assoc]

theorem identity_left (p : SourcePath) : compose (identity p.source) p = p := by
  cases p
  simp [compose, identity]

theorem identity_right (p : SourcePath) : compose p (identity p.target) = p := by
  cases p
  simp [compose, identity]

theorem composable_dagger {p q : SourcePath} (h : Composable p q) :
    Composable (dagger q) (dagger p) := by
  exact congrArg reverseBoundary h.symm

theorem flipStep_twice (s : Nat × Bool) : flipStep (flipStep s) = s := by
  cases s with
  | mk id direction => cases direction <;> rfl

theorem dagger_twice (p : SourcePath) : dagger (dagger p) = p := by
  cases p with
  | mk source target steps =>
    simp [dagger, reverseBoundary_twice, List.map_reverse, List.map_map,
      Function.comp_def, flipStep_twice]

theorem dagger_compose (p q : SourcePath) :
    dagger (compose p q) = compose (dagger q) (dagger p) := by
  simp [dagger, compose, List.reverse_append, List.map_append]

-- A path with no active register lanes remains a source path. Its existence
-- is carried independently of the register annotation.
structure AnnotatedPath where
  path : SourcePath
  reg : Reg16_3

def forgetRegister (p : AnnotatedPath) : SourcePath := p.path

theorem annotation_does_not_erase_path (p : SourcePath) (r : Reg16_3) :
    forgetRegister ⟨p, r⟩ = p := rfl

#print axioms compose_associative
#print axioms dagger_twice
#print axioms dagger_compose

end Imscribing.Biochem.PeptideSourcePaths
